body.html: Metha Palace is a mid-size Lanna-style hotel on Sakon Thawapi Road in the Dong Mafai area, right in central Sakon Nakhon. The first thing guests mention is the convenient, drive-anywhere location — roughly 1 km from the clock tower and night market, about 2-3 km from Wat Phra That Choeng Chum, and close to Big C and the in-town malls. That makes it a natural fit for anyone arriving by car or renting wheels to explore the province.

There are 35 rooms split between Standard and Deluxe categories with King, Twin and Queen beds. Every room has air-conditioning, a fridge and a flat-screen TV, and many add a private balcony. The most repeated praise in reviews is cleanliness — guests describe clean rooms, comfortable beds and good water pressure in the shower, which is exactly where hotels at this price point in the provinces often slip.
"Very clean room, comfy bed, strong water pressure, polite staff, and covered parking — for this price in Sakon city it's good value."

Another point road-trippers rate highly is the spacious covered parking. In a city where hotel parking is often tight, having a sheltered spot is a real plus. The front-desk staff also draw frequent compliments — reviewers call them polite, service-minded and happy to recommend places to eat and visit around town.

On the things to know before booking: parts of the building and some rooms are showing their age. A few reviews note that some bathroom fixtures are old and could be refreshed, and one guest compared the room feel to a student dormitory more than a smart hotel. And because rooms sit side by side, noise from neighbors can carry on some nights. This is a hotel that sells value and location, not design or polish.

On price, standard rooms here run roughly THB 450-650/night depending on dates and room type. During Sakon Nakhon's big festivals — the Wax Castle Procession and the end of Buddhist Lent in October — rates climb and rooms fill fast, so book ahead. Outside those peaks, the rate includes sheltered parking and free Wi-Fi, which is solid value for a clean bed in the city center.

The honest summary from real reviews: Metha Palace suits travelers arriving by car, here on business or sightseeing who won't spend much time in the room, and who value cleanliness, location and parking over a polished room. If you're expecting a brand-new property or a designer interior, look at other options in this roundup — but on pure value in Sakon city, this is a name guests come back to.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Metha Palace Sakon Nakhon

faq.q: Where is Metha Palace in Sakon Nakhon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Metha Palace is at 942 Sakon Thawapi Road, Dong Mafai, Mueang Sakon Nakhon, in the city center. It's about 1 km from the night market and clock tower, roughly 2.7 km from Wat Phra That Choeng Chum (a 5-7 minute drive), and close to Big C and the in-town malls — easy to drive anywhere.

faq.q: How much does Metha Palace cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 450/night for a Standard Queen. Deluxe rooms with a private balcony run about THB 590-650. Most regular-season rates fall in the THB 450-650 range depending on dates — always compare a few platforms before booking.
Yes — free covered parking is one of the most highly rated features, especially for self-drivers, since sheltered parking is limited at many central Sakon Nakhon hotels.

faq.q: Who is Metha Palace best for?
faq.a: It's a strong fit for travelers arriving by car, here on business or sightseeing who won't spend much time in the room and who value cleanliness, location and parking. If you want a brand-new, design-led hotel, look at other options, as the building is showing its age.

Around the Wax Castle Procession and end of Buddhist Lent (October), rooms fill fast and rates rise, so book several weeks ahead. In normal periods, 1-2 weeks is usually enough — pick a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't fixed.
